basis.text: The only writing of the time that names the barn, the Gettysburg Compiler of 20 Jul 1863, says it burned "while the battle was raging" with wounded Zouaves in it, which dates it after the fight of 2 Jul and within the battle. The Official Records name no Sherfy; later writers give 2 Jul (Miller 1909, Park Service 1981) or 3 Jul (Minnigh 1892), each without a source.

default.label: During the battle: from the Jul 2 afternoon fight (once wounded men were in the barn) to the end of Jul 3
default.basis_text: Lower bound: not before wounded men of the 114th Pennsylvania, who fought at the farm from the afternoon of 2 Jul, were in the barn (Compiler of 20 Jul 1863; 114th narrative); the fire may therefore fall during that fight, as the gunner in Moran's account allows ("during the cannonade", "while the battle was still on"), or after it. No source about the barn says which. Upper bound: the Compiler's "while the battle was raging" (the battle ended with 3 Jul). The two days inside the window are each given by one later text without a source.

animation.note: No single instant is supported: the barn stands until the window opens on the afternoon of 2 Jul and is shown burning, with "time uncertain" marked, anywhere in the window; the Jul 2 evening and Jul 3 readings stay selectable.

default.note: The hour is open. The plan's Jul 2 evening and Jul 3 are the two days inside the window.

witness.name: Robert C. Miller
witness.role: Gettysburg custodian and author of the text of "Historic Views of Gettysburg" (1909)

support.note: In a note under the view of the Sherfy house: "The house shows the marks of hundreds of bullets, while the old barn was burned during the battle of the second day." It says the day, not the hour, and gives no source.

support.quote: Since the first two were burned during the battle (Sherfy [...] on July 2 and Spangler's also on July 2)

witness.name: Kathleen R. Georg
witness.role: Research Historian, Gettysburg National Military Park

support.note: A footnote-free aside in a study of Pickett's division, written to decide which barn Major Haskell meant. It states that Sherfy's barn burned on 2 Jul and Spangler's also on 2 Jul and cites no source for either date. The text layer prints "Sherfy1s" for "Sherfy's".

support.quote: In the barn of the latter, and [...] stacks, were about twenty

witness.name: Gettysburg Compiler
witness.role: Weekly newspaper of Gettysburg, local notice in the issue of 20 Jul 1863 (unsigned)

support.note: The same notice, the sentence after the list of barn owners (the last owner in the list reads "Joseph SheTfy" in the damaged text layer, taken as Joseph Sherfy; "the latter" is that owner): about twenty wounded Philadelphia Zouaves "perished in the conflagration" in Sherfy's barn and around his hay stacks. The Zouaves were the 114th Pennsylvania, which fought at the farm on 2 Jul (Bowen; Hinman); this is why the fire is after the afternoon fight of 2 Jul, not before it.

support.quote: held the peach orchard until nearly dusk, when, finding the right unsupported, it fell back to the next ridge

witness.name: David B. Birney
witness.role: Major General, commanding First Division, Third Corps

support.note: Graham's brigade, which included the 114th and 57th Pennsylvania at the Sherfy buildings, held the Peach Orchard until "nearly dusk" and then fell back: the wounded left in the barn were left after that. Sunset on 2 Jul was 19:32 local mean time. Birney is a division commander and gives the time of the brigade, not of the barn.

inference.step: Miller (1909) and Georg (1981) give the day, 2 Jul, and no hour; the plan's "evening" is not in either. It is inferred from the Compiler (wounded Zouaves of the 114th were in the barn when it burned) and Birney (the brigade held the orchard until "nearly dusk"), which put the fire after the afternoon fight of 2 Jul.

reason_not_chosen.text: Two later texts give 2 Jul without a source and no text of the time gives a day; the one text that gives 3 Jul stands as high. Kept as the earliest day the record allows.

witness.name: Luther W. Minnigh
witness.role: Compiler of the guide book "Gettysburg: What They Did Here" (1892)

support.note: A one-line item in a collection of short notes; it says no hour, gives no source and says nothing about the 2d. The book prints the same line in its other editions (the second scan MINNIGH-1892-SCAN-B carries it too; one book, one group).

support.quote: I candidly believe it was I who caused his caissons to explode and set the barn on fire
support.note: Hart is describing 3 Jul (the paragraph begins "Early on the morning of the 3d" and follows the repulse of the infantry attack). He does not name the barn or its owner, and McMahon (OR27-1 p. 889, 17 Jul 1863) puts the battery that day "on the left of the cemetery". The quote says what Hart believes his guns did; it does not say that the barn is the Sherfy barn.

inference.step: Minnigh (1892) states the day, 3 Jul, without a source; Hart (15th New York Battery, 2 Aug 1863) claims on 3 Jul to have set "the barn" afire but does not name it. Hart is weighed as a possible fire of an unnamed barn on 3 Jul only (see P3); the Sherfy barn on that day rests on Minnigh alone.

reason_not_chosen.text: One later guide gives 3 Jul without a source; the Compiler of 1863 puts the fire only "while the battle was raging". Kept selectable as the latest day the record allows.

support.quote: a number of men as missing whom I have no doubt were killed and their bodies burned when the barn was burned down

witness.name: Edward R. Bowen
witness.role: Captain, 114th Pennsylvania Infantry (Graham's brigade, Third Corps), commanding the regiment after Cavada was taken

phrases: bodies burned when the barn was burned down

support.note: Bowen reports men missing from the fighting of 2 Jul that he assumes died in the barn; he does not name the barn or the owner, gives no hour and no day for the fire, and says "I have no doubt", so it is his belief. The report is compiled from his "own observations and memory" because he took the regiment only after Cavada was captured. The regiment fought at the Sherfy buildings on 2 Jul (Hinman, PA vol. 2).

support.page_note: printed page 616 (running head "616 Pennsylvania at Gettysburg.")
support.quote: Some of the wounded sought refuge in the barn, and being too badly wounded were not able to escape from it when it was burned and perished in the flames

witness.name: 114th Pennsylvania (Collis Zouaves) narrative
witness.role: Regimental account printed in "Pennsylvania at Gettysburg" (2d ed., 1914), vol. 2

support.note: The 114th Pennsylvania's own narrative, printed 51 years after the battle: wounded of the regiment sought refuge in the barn, could not escape when it was burned, and were buried as "unknown Zouaves". No day or hour for the fire. This ties the Zouaves of the Compiler to the 114th and to the afternoon fight of 2 Jul.

support.page_note: printed page 289 (the running head "290 CAMP AND FIELD" follows in the next sentence)
support.quote: The One Hundred and Fourteenth Pennsylvania, stretched along the Emmitsburg road from the gate of the Sherfy house and past the barn

witness.name: Frank E. Moran
witness.role: Captain, 73d New York ("Second Fire Zouaves"), Humphreys' division; captured wounded at the Sherfy buildings on 2 Jul

support.note: Moran describes the 114th Pennsylvania on the line of the Sherfy house and barn when his own regiment came up on the afternoon of 2 Jul: the regiment later said to have lost wounded in the barn stood beside it that afternoon.

support.page_note: printed page 296 (running head "296 CAMP AND FIELD" above the paragraph)
support.quote: Sherfy's barn had taken fire during the cannonade and was burned to the ground

witness.name: Frank E. Moran
witness.role: Captain, 73d New York ("Second Fire Zouaves"), Humphreys' division; captured wounded at the Sherfy buildings on 2 Jul

support.note: Moran (a prisoner, near Bunker Hill about ten days after the battle) reports what a soldier of the Washington Artillery told him, with a gap of 29 years: a man he "never saw before", whose name he cannot recall, said that his battery had engaged the line near the Sherfy house and that the barn took fire "during the cannonade". No day is given. Hearsay of hearsay: used only for the cause (shells) and for the fact that Confederates helped wounded men out.

support.page_note: printed page 296; the clause continues "while the battle Avas still on" in the text layer (Avas for was)
support.quote: who had crept into it for its doubtful shelter

witness.name: Frank E. Moran
witness.role: Captain, 73d New York ("Second Fire Zouaves"), Humphreys' division; captured wounded at the Sherfy buildings on 2 Jul

phrases: crept into it for its doubtful shelter

support.note: The same Washington Artillery soldier, as Moran reports him: wounded men, Union and Confederate, "who had crept into it for its doubtful shelter while the battle [was] still on" and could not escape "when the exploding shells set it on fire". Moran adds that two officers of a New York regiment were among those rescued; he took them to be his captain and a lieutenant of his own company.

support.quote: The bursting of shells had set fire to the large barn and destroyed it, burning at the same time a number of wounded soldiers who had sought refuge in it

witness.name: E. C. Strouss
witness.role: Member of the 57th Pennsylvania (Graham's brigade), author of chapter VIII of the regimental history (1900)

phrases: set fire to the large barn

support.note: Strouss walked out to the Sherfy house on the afternoon of 6 Jul and saw the burned barn; the chapter says the shells had set it afire. He gives no day for the fire, so the passage dates it only as before the afternoon of 6 Jul. Written 37 years after the visit.

support.quote: Mr. Sherfey's house on the right bears many scars of the battle. His barn was burned, and many bodies of dead Union soldiers were consumed with it.

witness.name: John B. Bachelder
witness.role: Battlefield historian and mapmaker; author of the guide "Gettysburg: What to See, and How to See It" (1873)

support.note: Bachelder, who surveyed the field for his maps, says the barn was burned with many dead Union soldiers in it. A footnote on the same page (printed p. 81) adds that a Confederate officer in hospital told him "he was personally in the barn immediately before it was burned" and that wounded men were not burned. No day or hour.

witness.role: Cultural Landscapes Inventory, Pickett's Charge Battlefield, Gettysburg National Military Park (2024)

support.note: The inventory says the battle-era barn was destroyed during the battle and used as a shelter for wounded Union soldiers, many of whom died in the fire; it gives no day or hour.

inference.step: The Gettysburg Compiler of 20 Jul 1863 says Sherfy's barn was among those burned "while the battle was raging" and that wounded Zouaves perished in it; those Zouaves (114th Pennsylvania, Bowen) fought at the farm on the afternoon of 2 Jul, so the fire is not before wounded men were in the barn, that is during that fight or after it (Birney, who says nothing of the barn, only dates the brigade's withdrawal at "nearly dusk"), and, the battle having ended with 3 Jul, before the end of that day. The window from 2 Jul to 3 Jul is that inference; no source of the time gives the day.

weighing.summary: No writing of the time dates the fire to a day. The Compiler (20 Jul 1863) puts it "while the battle was raging" with about twenty wounded Zouaves in the barn, and Bowen (13 Jul) assumes the missing men of 2 Jul were burned in it; both put it inside the battle and not before wounded men were in the barn (during the 2 Jul fight, as the gunner in Moran's account allows, or after it). Three later texts give a day: 2 Jul (Miller 1909; Georg 1981, no source) and 3 Jul (Minnigh 1892, no source). Hart (2 Aug 1863) claims to have set "a barn" afire on 3 Jul but does not name it. Nothing separates the two days, so the default is the window both days lie in.
weighing.who: The Compiler is a local weekly, the writer not on the field. Bowen commanded the 114th Pennsylvania that fought at the farm and was missing men, but took the regiment late and reports his belief ("I have no doubt"). Strouss saw the burned barn on 6 Jul and Bachelder wrote of it ten years on; neither gives a day. Moran heard it second-hand from a Confederate gunner. Minnigh, Miller and Georg are guide and park writers with no stated source; none of them stood at the farm. Hart saw a barn burn from the cemetery line and did not name it; his report of 2 Jul also mentions "the barn" (a column advancing on its left) without naming it, so his "barn" cannot be tied to Sherfy on either day, and the 3 Jul reading rests on Minnigh alone.
weighing.when: Best class: Bowen (13 Jul) and Hart (2 Aug) wrote official reports within a month, the Compiler 18 days after; but only the Compiler names the barn and none gives a day. The two writers that name a day wrote 29 years (Minnigh, 1892) and 46 years (Miller, 1909) after, and the Park Service study 118 years after; later history and institutional text rank below the reports and are used only for the day, as their claim.
weighing.where: Present at the farm on 2 Jul: Bowen (114th, which fell back from the brick house), Strouss and Moran (their regiments fought beside it; Moran was wounded and captured). Strouss walked out to the ruins on 6 Jul; Bachelder describes them in 1873. Not there: the Compiler, Minnigh, Miller, Georg. Hart fired from Cemetery Ridge on 3 Jul. The soldier Moran quotes was a gunner who engaged that line, but we hear him second-hand.
weighing.how_knew: No writer who stood at the farm says when it burned; Bowen and Strouss reason from the dead found. The day of Minnigh, Miller and Georg is a bare statement; where it comes from is unknown. Hart's statement is his belief about the effect of his own fire on a barn he does not name. The Compiler gives the fact and the Zouaves, not the day.
weighing.clock: Not applicable to the day; no source gives an hour or a Union or Confederate clock reading. The roughly 20-minute difference between the armies' clocks is not used.
weighing.independence: The Compiler, Bowen, the 114th Pennsylvania narrative, Moran, Strouss, Bachelder, the Park Service inventory and Birney are separate groups; none is seen to copy another, and all bear on the fire after the 2 Jul fight, none on the day. The three texts that give a day (Miller, Georg for 2 Jul; Minnigh for 3 Jul) cite nothing, so they may rest on local tradition and may share it; they disagree, so they are not counted as one line. Minnigh's two scans are one book. The plan's "Jul 2 evening" rests on no more than the unsourced lines of Miller and Georg: unproved, not disproved.

source_panel_text: Sometime in the battle, from the Jul 2 afternoon fight on: the Gettysburg Compiler of 20 Jul 1863 says Sherfy's barn burned "while the battle was raging" with about twenty wounded Zouaves in it. No text of the time gives the day; later books say Jul 2 (1909, 1981) or Jul 3 (1892), none with a source. Both days stay selectable; the hour is open.

pdf_default.note: Jul 2 evening is not disproved: two later texts give Jul 2 and the fire is after the afternoon fight. But no source gives "evening", and Jul 3 stands as high. It stays selectable as the earliest day the record allows.

first_delegated.note: The delegated marking as a gap is replaced: the Compiler of 20 Jul 1863, which the first pass did not read for the barn's fate, bounds the fire to the battle, from the time wounded men were in the barn on 2 Jul (inferred), so the record is divided on the day rather than empty. The delegated Jul 2 evening default is kept as a selectable position; the claim that no source names the barn was true only of the Official Records.

readers.note: Row window "Jul 2 ~18:00" and tier documented; its text says "July 2 evening (one account) vs July 3 during the afternoon artillery (most sources)". No source says "most sources" or the evening; the row should carry the window of this resolution and tier inferred.

Row says "Barn burns", Jul 3 afternoon-evening, tier documented and "Jul 3 afternoon most plausible (inferred)"; the resolution has no preference for the afternoon of 3 Jul. The Stone Sentinels reading it cites (standing on the morning of 3 Jul) was not read here.

The default fire scenario is read on 3 Jul and the Jul 2 scenario covers 2 Jul only; the default of this resolution is a window from 2 Jul to 3 Jul with no instant, which is the existing flag_window_full scenario.
